scarpa: Founded 1938 in Asolo, Italy. Nearly a century of handmade mountain footwear, still family-run.
la sportiva: Founded 1928 by Narciso Delladio in the Italian Dolomites. Family-owned for nearly 100 years of mountain footwear.
five ten: Founded 1985 in California by Charles Cole. Its Stealth rubber set the benchmark for climbing-shoe grip.
evolv: Founded 2003 in Southern California. Built by climbers around shoes designed and tested on US rock.
butora: Founded 2014 in South Korea. A young brand that earned its following through fit-focused construction.
mad rock: Founded 2002 in California by Young Chu. Built its name on technical shoes at accessible prices.
black diamond: Grew out of Chouinard Equipment (founded 1957); formed 1989 after Yvon Chouinard's original company collapsed. Based in Salt Lake City.
ocun: Founded 1994 in Přerov, Czech Republic as Rock Pillars; renamed Ocún in 2007.
red chili: Founded 1996 in Germany by pro climber Stefan Glowacz and Uwe Hofstädter.
so ill: Founded 2002 in St. Louis by brothers Daniel and Jason Chancellor. Independent brand known for design-driven, colorful gear.
tenaya: Founded 1997 by José Luis García Gallego in Alicante, Spain — a region with a deep shoemaking tradition.
unparallel: Founded 2017 in Southern California by Sang Lee and former Five Ten designers. Locally built performance shoes.
edelrid: Founded 1863 in Germany — one of climbing's oldest companies. Invented the kernmantle rope before moving into footwear.
salewa: Founded 1935 in Munich, now rooted in Italy's South Tyrol. Nearly a century of alpine equipment.
zamberlan: Founded 1929 by Giuseppe Zamberlan in Italy. Third-generation family bootmaker for mountain terrain.
boreal: Founded 1975 by Jesús García López in Villena, Spain — part of Alicante's shoemaking heartland.
rock pillars: Czech climbing brand founded 1994; relaunched as Ocún in 2007.
simond: Founded 1860 in the Chamonix valley, France — one of mountaineering's oldest names; now Decathlon's climbing brand.
